analysis:
Examined all supplied prefix-cache documentation excerpts and the bounded patch. The visible changes add Gemma TP to tenant-scoped resident/SSD paths (docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md, head patch lines 1043–1044) and describe incremental request-row reservation through reservedTokens (head patch lines 1078–1084). Neither establishes a concrete security regression: the text preserves authenticated partitioning, fresh request-owned rows and release on restoration failure. The update date at head line 3 has no security effect. Surrounding BASE documentation describes bilateral restore confirmation, media cache exclusion, encrypted per-rank storage, bounded write queues and identity binding; these are documentation claims, not verification of runtime controls.
Relevant contracts are A-001/T-041/TB-007 for tenant isolation, at-rest prefix confidentiality and timing exposure, and availability/resource ownership at the inference boundary. Integration should verify Gemma4TensorParallelPrefix.scopes carries the authenticated partition into both tiers and that reservedTokens retains charge-before-allocation, growth limits and failure/cancellation cleanup in CBv2PagedPrefixRestore and its changed callers. No changed implementation is supplied here. The added head section at lines 1267–1320 is also absent from these excerpts and the patch is truncated, so its behavior and any material threat-model updates remain unreviewed in this pass. The earlier resident/SSD descriptions must not be treated as new PR regressions merely because they differ from historical T-041 prose.
